apps/desktop/electron/services/matter-br.content: `stop()` kills the process and nulls `this.port`, but the port's `onExit` handler (registered in `start()`) fires asynchronously and unconditionally calls `this.start()`. Because there is no `stopped`/lifecycle flag, a `stop()` issued while a running controller is killed will respawn the utility process right after intentional shutdown, leaving an orphaned/zombie process that the service no longer tracks. Add a `stopped` flag (set in `stop()`, cleared in `start()`) or a generation token that `onExit` checks before restarting.

The exit closure is not bound to the specific `port` instance, so an exit event from a previously replaced or killed port will null out `this.port` (which may already point to a freshly started port) and then call `this.start()`, spawning a duplicate controller while orphaning the live one. Capture `port` in the closure and guard with `if (this.port !== port) return;` before clearing/restarting.

`this.restarts` is never reset, so it accumulates across the entire process lifetime. After `maxRestarts` crashes spread over months (even with long healthy runs in between), the bridge is permanently pinned to `degraded` with no way to recover. Reset the counter after a healthy uptime window (e.g. the process stayed alive for N seconds) or expose an explicit reset so transient crashes don't cause permanent degradation.

`postMessage` is called with no error handling. If the controller process has crashed but `onExit` hasn't run yet (the exit is asynchronous), `this.port` is still non-null and `postMessage` throws a raw exception to the caller, contradicting the `boolean` contract that implies `false` on failure. Wrap the call in try/catch and return `false` on failure.

A throwing listener aborts delivery to the remaining listeners and propagates the exception into the port's message callback (potentially killing message dispatch entirely). Wrap each invocation in try/catch so one faulty subscriber cannot break message relay for others.

Options are only applied on the first invocation (`instance ??= new MatterBridge(opts)`). Any later caller passing `spawn` or `maxRestarts` is silently ignored, which can yield a non-functional bridge that never wires the utility process. Document that options are first-call-only, or merge/override options on subsequent calls.
